Italian Republic (ICSID Case No. ARB/18/20) September 15, 2026 Petersen Energia S.A.U. ...' - analytics/fetch-results/2026-09-17-zz-controls-and-databases.json idx 2, find 'ARB/', find_matched true, 362,583 bytes; the same string recurs at 2026-09-17-zzz-class-predicate-cure.json idx 1 and at 2026-10-10-daily.json idx 4 (363,110 bytes). WHY IT IS FATAL TO THE UNIFORM READING, which is thread 66's own statement of the problem: the 2026-10-11 batch's maximum-lookbehind row returned the sort strip verbatim - 'Pending Cases Concluded Cases Recent Cases Recent Cases Registered Published Concluded Constituted October 6, 2026 Lombard ...' - FOUR date-type labels, NO case-name header, each entry's date rendering BEFORE its name. On that reading 'September 16, 2026' binds to ARB/18/20, and an ARB/18/xx designator is not a 2026 registration. So either the page is a union of four recency feeds in which each entry carries the date of the event that put it there, or the date-before-name binding is wrong. UNTIL IT IS SETTLED, NO DATE ON /cases/recent MAY BE READ AS A REGISTRATION DATE - that prohibition is in force now and this batch does not lift it; only a reading of these rows can. PRIOR ART ON THIS EXACT URL, SCREENED BEFORE WRITING (prior-art screen on instrument claims, thread 51): this page has been fetched ONCE, on 2026-09-18 (2026-09-18-daily.json idx 7), find 'Subject of Dispute', find_matched TRUE, ok/200/text-html, 103,808 bytes, returning ICSID's own labelled triple verbatim: 'Subject of Dispute: Renewable energy generation enterprise Economic Sector: Electric Power & Other Energy Instrument(s) Invoked: (i) ECT (Energy Charter Treaty) Applicable Rules: ICSID Convention'. TWO CONSEQUENCES, both load-bearing. (i) THE UNENCODED URL FORM 'CaseNo=ARB/18/20' IS CERTIFIED 200 ON THIS HOST by that row, so every row below uses it; the percent-encoded form has never been fired on this matter and is not used here. (ii) THE MATTER IS AN ECT RENEWABLE-ENERGY MATTER WITH NO IP, PHARMACEUTICAL, TRADE-SECRET OR CLINICAL-DATA NEXUS WHATEVER. THIS BATCH IS THEREFORE NOT RESEARCH INTO THE RESEARCH QUESTION AND MAY NEVER BE WRITTEN UP AS SUCH. It is an instrument-calibration batch whose entire product is a rule about how to read dates on /cases/recent. No seat may convert any row below into a finding about intellectual property as a covered investment, about any ring, or about Italy, Veolia or the Energy Charter Treaty. LITERAL-ATTESTATION CENSUS, run over all 586 prior relay rows before choosing the finds below, so no row is a guess: on case-detail URLs 'Status of Proceeding' is 62/62 TRUE, 'Subject of Dispute' is 30/30 TRUE, 'Published Decisions' is 6/10, and 'Date Registered' is 0/1 - its one firing was on UNCT/20/6 (2026-09-05-daily.json idx 3, ok/200, 105,703 bytes, find_matched FALSE), a DIFFERENT page family. The literal is nonetheless attested in VISIBLE PROSE on ARB-family Convention pages, inside windows cut by other finds: 'Date Registered: January 12, 2012' on ARB/12/1 (2026-09-01-daily.json idx 2, find 'Composition of Tribunal'; and idx 5 of 2026-09-02-daily.json, find 'Claimant(s)/Nationality(ies)') and 'Date Registered: December 8, 2025' on ARB/24/16 (2026-09-13-daily.json idx 2, find 'Outcome'). SO ROW 2 IS A FIRST FIRING OF A LITERAL WITH ONE PRIOR FALSE ON ANOTHER PAGE FAMILY, and a FALSE on row 2 is an INSTRUMENT OBSERVATION about label rendering on this page, NEVER a statement that the matter has no registration date. NOTE ON MULTIPLE OCCURRENCES, binding on how row 2 is read: excerpt_of searches with body.lower().find() (scripts/fetch_relay.py:131), which returns the FIRST occurrence only. 'Date Registered' occurs more than once on pages carrying annulment or revision proceedings - ARB/12/1 renders it at January 12, 2012 for the original proceeding and again at November 18, 2019 for the annulment and March 16, 2021 for the revision. Row 2 therefore returns the FIRST such label in document order and nothing about any later one. If the window's date is a 2018 date the original-proceeding reading is corroborated by document order; if it is not, NO INFERENCE is available about which proceeding it belongs to without a further row, and none may be drawn. WHAT EACH OUTCOME WOULD AND WOULD NOT SETTLE, FIXED HERE BEFORE THE ROWS FIRE. (A) If row 2 returns a 2018 registration date AND row 3 ('September 16, 2026') returns TRUE with that date adjacent to a labelled event on this page, then the date-before-name binding on /cases/recent HOLDS and the page is confirmed a union of feeds in which the date is the date of whichever feed event listed the entry - and the standing prohibition hardens into a permanent rule rather than lifting, because the row itself still does not say WHICH feed listed any given entry. (B) If row 2 returns a 2018 date and row 3 returns FALSE while row 4 hits, then 'September 16, 2026' is absent from this matter's own 100-kilobyte page while being rendered next to its name on /cases/recent, and the date-before-name binding is IMPEACHED - which kills the technique, exactly as thread 66 says it might. (C) If rows 1-4 all miss, the batch is UNINTERPRETABLE as to this page and goes back as an instrument observation. NO OTHER READING IS AUTHORISED, and in particular no row below founds a count, a rate, an ordinal fact, or any statement about how ICSID populates any feed. A FALSE ON A DATE LITERAL IS FORM-SPECIFIC AND CASE-INSENSITIVE: the find is case-insensitive (:131) but exact as to form, so a page rendering '16 September 2026' or 'Sept. 16, 2026' would not match row 3, and a null is a null ON THIS FORM at the batch instant. urls.purpose: THE PRE-REGISTERED CLOSURE ROW FOR THREAD 66, fired in the exact form that thread fixed on 2026-10-11. Prior art: 62 of 62 prior relay rows with this find on case-detail URLs returned find_matched TRUE. Expected TRUE. WHAT IT FOUNDS: ICSID's own labelled statement of this matter's procedural status as rendered at the batch instant, plus whatever the forward 300 characters of the window carry - on ARB/12/1 and ARB/24/16 that same window carried 'Outcome of Proceeding: <date> - The Tribunal renders its award' and the opening of an '(b) Annulment Proceeding' block with its own 'Date Registered', so this row may well return the dated event that explains a September 2026 listing. WHAT IT DOES NOT FOUND: any holding, any reasoning, any disposition beyond the labelled text itself - G16 bars a docket-summary surface from founding a disposition and G10 bars reading a document designation as a tribunal's characterisation.

THE DISCRIMINATOR. A 2018 original-proceeding registration date on this page is what makes 'September 16, 2026' on /cases/recent provably NOT a registration date for this entry. Prior art is mixed and is stated honestly: this literal is 0/1 as a fired find, its one firing being on UNCT/20/6 (a different page family) where it returned FALSE against a live 200; but it IS attested in visible prose on ARB-family Convention pages inside other finds' windows ('Date Registered: January 12, 2012' on ARB/12/1; 'Date Registered: December 8, 2025' on ARB/24/16). Expected TRUE, with a real chance of FALSE. Returns the FIRST occurrence in document order only. A FALSE IS AN INSTRUMENT OBSERVATION about label rendering on this page and is NEVER a statement that this matter has no registration date.

THE BINDING ROW, page-wide. excerpt_of searches the WHOLE tag-stripped, whitespace-collapsed body (scripts/fetch_relay.py:131) before any window is cut, so this row tests the entire rendering - approximately 103,808 bytes on the 2026-09-18 reading - for this exact date literal, and its window would show the labelled event the date sits beside. NEVER FIRED on this URL. A TRUE binds the /cases/recent date to a named event on the matter's own page and corroborates the date-before-name binding; a FALSE, given that row 4 hits, IMPEACHES that binding and kills the technique. Either way the product is a rule about reading a docket surface, not a fact about any matter.

SAME-RUN CONTROL, required by analytics/fetch-requests/README.md because row 3 may legitimately return a null and excerpt_of returns the empty string on a miss (:132-133), leaving a null row with no window at all. REGION-SCOPED AND ATTESTED ON THIS VERY URL: find_matched TRUE here on 2026-09-18 at 103,808 bytes, and 30 of 30 across all case-detail rows. Expected TRUE. It establishes that the origin answered and that the tag-strip yielded labelled field prose from THIS byte stream, which is what makes a null on row 3 interpretable. It also re-reads the 'Instrument(s) Invoked' field at no extra cost - the free one-field structural screen adopted 2026-10-11 - and a second reading of it 24 days later is how a changed field would be caught. A FALSE here voids the reading of row 3's null.

FEED-IDENTIFICATION ROW. The sort strip on /cases/recent names four date types - Registered, Published, Concluded, Constituted - and if this entry was listed by the Published feed then a decision was published on or about September 16, 2026 and this section is where ICSID says so. Prior art is the weakest of the five finds and is stated as such: 6 of 10 prior firings on case-detail URLs returned TRUE, so a FALSE here is well within the instrument's known behaviour and founds nothing. WHAT A TRUE FOUNDS: the titles and dates of documents ICSID itself lists as published in this matter, as rendered at the batch instant. WHAT IT DOES NOT FOUND: the content of any such document, which this instrument cannot read (excerpt_of returns '' for PDFs, :124), and no URL for any document, since the tag-strip destroys every href.

THE REMAINING FEED LIMB, and the cheapest way to leave only one feed unaccounted for. If the entry was listed by the Constituted feed, a tribunal or committee constitution dated September 16, 2026 is the explanation, and this is the label ICSID uses for it. Prior art: this exact literal has never been fired as a find, but it is attested in visible prose on ARB/12/1 ('Date of Constitution of Tribunal: July 12, 2012', inside the 'Composition of Tribunal' window, 2026-09-01-daily.json idx 2), and its ad hoc Committee sibling 'Date of Constitution of ad hoc Committee' is 2/2 TRUE. Expected TRUE as a label. Returns the FIRST occurrence in document order; a page carrying both an original tribunal and a later reconstitution gives up only the first, and no inference about the others is authorised. A FALSE is an instrument observation, not a statement that no tribunal was constituted.
